display.purpose: The masthead H1 only, once per page. Capped at 22ch. A fluid clamp, one of the two sanctioned font-size literals in a rule.

headline.purpose: The H2 opening each band — the pipeline stage's name. The second sanctioned fluid clamp.

title.purpose: Ramp step --t-2xl (1.4rem). A scene's detected summary and the drop-zone title, which used to be a 1.35rem one-off.

subtitle.purpose: Ramp step --t-xl (1.2rem). A candidate's one-line summary at 700 (formerly a 1.12rem one-off) and a fieldset legend at 800.

body.purpose: Ramp step --t-base. All prose; secondary prose drops to --t-sm in Ink Soft. The step above, --t-lg, carries UI strings that need a little more weight: masthead sub-line, rail step name, fact term, sub-form legend, dock title, clip title, primary button.

label.purpose: Ramp step --t-xs. Field labels, elapsed clock, clip ids, rod roles. Sentence case, never uppercase or letter-spaced.

numeral.purpose: The number inside a rod bar, plus every tabular figure a teacher compares against their own deck: file names, slide tags, ids, grades, the clock.

shadows.name: block
shadows.purpose: The default lift: bands, clip cards, the active rail step, any hovered button. Offset riser plus a real blur.

shadows.name: raised
shadows.purpose: The fixed render dock only — the single element that floats above the page.

shadows.name: inset
shadows.purpose: The dark video well, so slate reads as recessed rather than as a dark card.

motion.name: ease
motion.purpose: The only easing in the system. Fast out, long settle — things arrive and seat.

motion.name: duration-state
motion.purpose: Pick-row border/background changes (0.18s), drop-zone hover (0.25s), rail step background-color (0.35s).

motion.name: seat
motion.purpose: The active rail step dropping into place when a stage advances.

motion.name: spin
motion.purpose: The working mark on in-progress stamps and dock rows. Disabled under prefers-reduced-motion.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.value: transition-duration: 0.01ms !important on *; seat and spin animations set to none
motion.purpose: prefers-reduced-motion: reduce kills every transition and both keyframe animations globally.

textures.name: tooth
textures.value: inline SVG feTurbulence, fractalNoise baseFrequency 0.9, numOctaves 4, saturate 0, rect at opacity 0.28
textures.purpose: The paper material. Applied to exactly four surfaces: .shell::before (0.5 opacity, mix-blend-mode multiply), .band, .drop, .rail__step. State changes on any of these must use background-color, never the background shorthand.

fonts.name: Baloo 2
fonts.value: /fonts/baloo2-var.woff2, woff2-variations, weight axis 400–800, font-display swap, preloaded
fonts.purpose: Display face. Self-hosted variable woff2; no third-party font host.

fonts.name: Rubik
fonts.value: /fonts/rubik-var.woff2, woff2-variations, weight axis 300–900, font-display swap, preloaded
fonts.purpose: UI face. Self-hosted variable woff2; no third-party font host.

tokenDiscipline.name: literal-free rules
tokenDiscipline.value: 62 custom properties on :root; zero literal hex values and zero literal border-radius values in any rule outside :root
tokenDiscipline.purpose: Verified by script over the stylesheet. A literal in a rule is a bug, not a shortcut.

tokenDiscipline.name: sanctioned exceptions
tokenDiscipline.value: body font-size 16px (the root the rem ramp measures against); clamp(2.1rem, 5vw, 3.4rem) and clamp(1.45rem, 2.6vw, 1.9rem) display sizes; rgba(26, 28, 33, 0.28) on the rod bar edge
tokenDiscipline.purpose: The display clamps must scale with the viewport and a fixed ramp step cannot. The rod edge is an alpha of Ink so one border darkens all ten rod fills — an alpha of an existing token is the only acceptable inline colour.

accessibility.name: focus-ring
accessibility.value: :focus-visible { outline: 3px solid var(--action); outline-offset: 2px; border-radius: var(--r-xs) }
accessibility.purpose: Global, never removed. A component's focus border shift is an addition to this ring, never a replacement.

accessibility.name: sr-only
accessibility.value: position: absolute; width: 1px; height: 1px; padding: 0; margin: -1px; overflow: hidden; clip: rect(0,0,0,0); white-space: nowrap; border: 0
accessibility.purpose: Carries the state word beside every decorative icon: rail steps, stamps, dock rows.

accessibility.name: live-region
accessibility.value: aria-live="polite" on the dock heading; aria-hidden on the elapsed clock
accessibility.purpose: Only the render heading announces. The clock mutates every second and would talk over everything else.

narrative.overview:
This is the warm butcher-paper wall of a K-8 classroom, not a dashboard. The ground is off-white stock with real tooth in it; colour arrives as hard-edged fields that own whole regions rather than as tints sprinkled on cards. The system's central claim is that colour here is a working code — the Cuisenaire rod set every K-8 maths teacher already owns — so a colour is never chosen to set a mood or to distinguish a category. It is chosen because a number is 7.

Density is generous and single-column. Depth is plastic sitting on paper: a low offset riser plus a real blur, the way a moulded block casts a soft shadow on a sheet, never the flat zero-blur slab of a neobrutalist poster. Type is one friendly rounded display face carrying every heading, with a clean geometric UI face for everything a teacher reads or types; there is no third voice.

The world refuses two things by name. It refuses the pastel edtech dashboard — rounded lavender cards, mint chips, colour as reassurance — because pastel cannot carry a rod law. And it refuses the dark video-editor opposite: dark exists here in exactly one place, as a local inset behind a thumbnail or clip so the rendered video is the brightest thing on screen. Dark is a material for showing video, not a theme.

The system is fully tokenized: all 62 custom properties are declared on :root, and no rule outside :root carries a literal hex colour, a literal border-radius, or an off-ramp font-size. Three deliberate exceptions are named in the sections below. A literal in a rule is a bug in this system, not a shortcut.
keyCharacteristics: Colour encodes value 1–10, never category or mood
Warm paper ground with real SVG-noise tooth on every stock surface
One card level; nested grouping is a tinted block with a hairline rule
Depth is offset plus real blur; zero-blur block shadows are banned
Baloo 2 at 800 over Rubik, self-hosted variable woff2, preloaded
One six-step type ramp; no font-size literals in rules
Progress is discrete and countable; percentages are forbidden
Dark is a local inset for video only

rules.name: The Rod Law
rules.body: Colour binds to a value, 1 through 10, and never to a category. A 7 is near-black wherever it appears. Integers outside 1–10 have no rod in the physical set, so they get no colour here either — rodFor() returns null and the value renders without a bar. Rod width encodes magnitude on the same axis (value × 9%, so a 10 spans 90%), which means a rod is legible as quantity even in greyscale.

rules.name: The Neutral Category Rule
rules.body: Anything that names a kind stays board-neutral. Template chips carry a data-template attribute and there is deliberately no CSS that reads it — the hook exists so the neutrality is visible as a choice rather than an omission. If a category ever borrowed a rod hue, the rod law would stop being readable.

rules.name: The Pale-Rod Ink Rule
rules.body: Rods 1, 3, 5 and 10 take dark numerals; every other rod takes on-action white. This is a fixed set (ROD_DARK_INK), not a computed guess.

rules.name: The Role-Separation Rule
rules.body: Semantic colour and rod colour are separated by role, not by hue — and the stylesheet's own header now says so. A semantic hue never becomes a bar, never carries a numeral, and never appears inside the rod list; a rod hue never reports a state. Each semantic ink is in fact a darker, lower-chroma sibling of its nearest rod (ok sits ~2° from Rod 6, danger ~1° from Rod 2, fallback <1° from Rod 8, action ~8° from Rod 9), separated by 8–14 points of lightness. Never "fix" this by moving a semantic hue — the semantics are readable because they are always darker and always in a different job.

rules.name: The Local Dark Rule
rules.body: Dark is a material, not a theme. Slate appears only as the inset behind a thumbnail, a clip, or a preview-unavailable message, so rendered video reads as the brightest object on the page. Never a dark shell, never a dark card, never a dark band.

rules.name: The Named Tint Rule
rules.body: Every fill, hover, border tint and ink belongs to a named family before it is used. The pale blues are the worked example: the build once spelled them three ways as literals, and they resolved not into one ramp but into an action pair (action-field behind an icon, action-field-soft under a selected row) plus a reassignment of the third to a different family entirely (teach-field). Naming a tint is what reveals which family it belongs to. One deliberate literal remains in a rule: the rod bar's 2px edge is rgba(26, 28, 33, 0.28) — Ink at 28% alpha, so the edge darkens whatever rod hue sits under it instead of fighting ten different fills. An alpha of an existing token is the only acceptable inline colour.

rules.name: The One Ramp Rule
rules.body: There is one type ramp of six steps (--t-xs .85 / --t-sm .93 / --t-base 1 / --t-lg 1.06 / --t-xl 1.2 / --t-2xl 1.4 rem) and no font-size literal in any rule. The two exceptions are structural, not stylistic: the root body size (16px) that the rem ramp is measured against, and the two fluid display clamp() values, which exist because a masthead and a band heading must scale with the viewport and a fixed step cannot. Everything else — including the sizes that used to be 1.12rem and 1.35rem one-offs — sits on a step. A new UI size is a bug, not a decision.

rules.name: The Tabular Numeral Rule
rules.body: Any number a teacher might compare against their own deck gets font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums. Numbers must not reflow horizontally as they change.

rules.name: The One Expressive Voice Rule
rules.body: Baloo 2 sets headings, legends, rod numerals, chips and stage names. It never sets body prose, error text, or a source excerpt — the moment it does, the extracted values start looking illustrated.

rules.name: The Measure Rule
rules.body: Every prose block is capped in ch, tightening as the text gets less important: 22ch for the display headline, 42–46ch for hint and definition text, 62–74ch for notes, excerpts and rationales. No paragraph runs the full 1080px. Where a label cannot wrap at all — a dock row's template · ids — it is capped in rem and truncated with an ellipsis instead, so a long template name never reflows the bar.

rules.name: The Gutter Decoration Rule
rules.body: Decorative shapes live outside the content column or behind it at z-index: 0; content and the masthead sit at z-index: 1. When the column claims the gutter, the decoration moves out of the way rather than sliding under the text.

rules.name: The Real-Blur Rule
rules.body: A shadow is an offset riser plus a real blur. A zero-blur block shadow is banned outright: it is the tell of a different world and this one is paper, not poster board.

rules.name: The One Card Level Rule
rules.body: The band is the card, and it is the only card. A group inside a band is a tinted block — no border, no radius, no shadow — set off by a 1px top rule and vertical space (the scene block), or by a legend and a 0.9rem indent (the schema sub-form). A third nesting level does not exist. The one exception is state: an approved or rejected scene takes the mid radius and its semantic field colour, because that is a status, not a container.

rules.name: The Hover-Lift Rule
rules.body: Buttons translate −1px and gain the Block shadow on hover, then return to 0 on :active — press is the absence of lift. Nothing scales on hover.

rules.name: The Tooth Rule
rules.body: --tooth — an inline feTurbulence SVG at 0.28 opacity — is the paper material, and it is applied to exactly four surfaces: the shell overlay (0.5 opacity, mix-blend-mode multiply), the band, the drop zone, and the rail step. On any toothed surface, state changes must use background-color, never the background shorthand — the shorthand resets background-image and silently strips the texture.

rules.name: The No Side-Tab Rule
rules.body: No element carries a coloured left or right accent border. The build contains no border-left/border-right declaration at all, which is the enforcement: state is carried by fill, by a full 2px border, or by text — never by a stripe down one edge.

dos: Do bind colour to value through the rod law (--rod-1..--rod-10) and let width carry magnitude (value × 9%), so a rod survives greyscale.
Do keep every category label — template chips above all — on Board Deep neutral.
Do flip rod numerals to dark ink on rods 1, 3, 5 and 10; every other rod takes --on-action.
Do name a tint before you use it. Every colour in a rule is a var(), and a new fill, hover or border tint joins a family (-field, -field-soft, -line) rather than appearing as a literal.
Do take every size from the six-step ramp and every corner from the four-step radius family.
Do use background-color on any surface that carries --tooth; the background shorthand wipes the texture.
Do pair every offset riser with a real blur (--shadow-block, --shadow-raised).
Do report progress as discrete, countable, all-reachable stages, and name the honest expectation in words ("This takes minutes, not seconds").
Do append an sr-only state word next to every decorative icon, mark decorative SVG aria-hidden with focusable="false", and put aria-current="step" on the active rail step.
Do treat the labeled text-card fallback as a success: notice--fallback, warm brown, its reason stated.
Do keep the global 3px --action focus ring and add to it — a focus border shift is an addition, never a swap.
Do author icons at one 2px stroke with square caps and currentColor.
Do give a failure a real recovery path in place (a danger notice with its own actions), and say what was preserved.
donts: Don't show a percentage, a determinate bar, or an ETA for rendering. POST /render is one blocking batch call with no progress stream, so any number would be fabricated. Discrete stamps and an elapsed clock only.
Don't let a rod hue report a state, or a semantic hue become a bar or carry a numeral. Role separation is the whole mechanism.
Don't paint a rod for a value outside integer 1–10 — that rod does not exist in the physical set.

Don't write a literal hex, border-radius or font-size in a rule. The only sanctioned exceptions are the two fluid display clamp() sizes, the root 16px body size, and an rgba() alpha of an existing token (the rod bar's edge).
Don't use a zero-blur block shadow.
Don't take the shell dark, or apply --slate to anything but a video or thumbnail well.
Don't add a coloured left or right accent border. There is no side-tab in this system at any width.
Don't add a third container level. Nest by tinted block, hairline rule, legend and indent.

Don't convey an inactive or lesser state by lowering the opacity of text — it was tried on the todo rail step and dropped the index to 2.8:1 against the board. Use a paler fill (--board-quiet) instead.
Don't style the fallback as an error, and don't use danger for anything that is not a genuine failure.
Don't let decoration overlap a validated number, an extracted value, or a source excerpt; the playful layer stays at z-index: 0 and pointer-events: none.
Don't show the platform's own file-input widget; the styled label is the control.
Don't uppercase or letter-space UI labels.
Don't announce a ticking value in a live region.
